newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1996 retail inflation up 6.1 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 retail inflation up 6.1 pct yr/yr.

text.p: China's retail price inflation rose by 6.1 percent in 1996, down sharply from an inflation rate of 14.48 percent in 1995, the State Statistical Bureau said on Tuesday.
Consumer price inflation rose 8.3 percent for the year, the bureau said.
The report estimated that the benchmark retail price inflation would remain at a similar level in 1997.
The cost of services rose by 16 percent while food prices grew 7.6 percent, the bureau said in a report issued by the Xinhua news agency.
The price of grain rose by 6.5 percent while eggs rose by 16.5 percent year-on-year and fresh vegetables were up 19.7 percent.

The southern and eastern provinces of Hainan, Guangdong and Fujian and the southwestern Guangxi region all showed an annual retail price increase of less than 4.5 percent, making them the most successful regions in curbing inflation, it said.
The highest increases were in the westernmost Xinjiang region where prices rose by 8.8 percent and in north-central Shaanxi province where inflation was 8.1 percent, it said.
Retail prices in rural areas continued to rise more quickly than in urban areas, increasing by 6.4 percent year-on-year, about 0.6 percentage points above urban areas.
Prices in 1996 for farm materials rose 8.4 percent, the lowest increase in three years, it said.
